We take the fallback rather than preferred, leaving Vendor's ownership of Deliverables and its generic tools and know-how intact, and simply upgrade the licence sentence.

The preferred level is not reached and was not claimed: Vendor still exclusively owns Deliverables with no assignment to Customer, and the irrevocable/royalty-free character of the embedded Vendor Technology licence depends on Section 13.2, which is not in evidence. Minimality holds. Only the second sentence of 14.2 is rewritten; 14.1 and 14.3 are preserved verbatim, including the Customer-favourable identification and third-party-material approval duties. quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
rationale: Section 21 satisfies our preferred position on all material terms and comfortably clears the fallback. The cap is expressly mutual ("The cap is mutual"), set at the greater of Fees paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000; "Fees" (§1.5) covers recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the basis is not illusory. Section 21.2 excludes indirect and consequential damages mutually (and helpfully confirms data restoration, replacement services, notices and incident response are direct damages). Section 21.3's Excluded Claims sit outside the cap and cover confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's IP. Section 21.4 preserves liability that cannot lawfully be limited and survives failure of an exclusive remedy. No competing or one-sided cap appears elsewhere (the only other "liability" references are Vendor's insurance covenants in §18.1). The one shortfall from preferred wording is that the payment carve-out in §21.3 is limited to "undisputed Fees for conforming Services" rather than all Customer amounts due; that narrowing operates in our favour (it keeps disputed and non-Fee amounts inside the cap rather than exposing us to uncapped payment claims), so we note it rather than redline it. No redline proposed.

The only wording short of the ideal preferred formulation is that the competitor bar is limited to a "direct" competitor and is expressed as subject to our own consent — a minor sub-element noted here rather than redlined, since Vendor assignment already requires our consent in all cases. No redline proposed.

The only friction is §14.2, which describes the Deliverable licence as "revocable, non-transferable" and conflicts with §§13.2–13.3; consistent with the playbook we address revocability of Deliverable/IP rights once under the IP rule rather than flagging the same commercial term twice here.

The tail "or to give Vendor most-favoured-customer terms" overlaps in substance with the Section 12.3 acknowledgment, but it restates the very element under review rather than adding an out-of-checklist requirement, so it does not defeat minimality; a pure deletion would have been marginally tighter. elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: "indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs, and expenses".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "Vendor's breach of Applicable Law", tracking the defined term in Section 1.2.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "any unauthorized access to, or disclosure of, Customer Data caused by Vendor".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Limb (d): "Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "Customer shall give Vendor prompt written notice of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "Vendor shall control the defence of the claim" — control expressly allocated to Vendor.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: "Customer shall provide reasonable cooperation".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: "Customer's indemnity obligations under this Agreement, if any, are limited to third-party claims arising out of Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law."

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Same inserted limb (a) covers third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims regarding the Services or Deliverables.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no Customer-modification exclusion was added, and none is required; the absence is Customer-favourable, so the condition does not apply.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination exclusion inserted, which is more favourable to Customer than the fallback contemplates.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no specification exclusion inserted, so nothing to satisfy.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph contains no procure/modify/replace remedy; Section 9.3 still points to "the remedies required by Section 20.5", which does not exist in the rendered text.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees backstop tied to unavailability of procure/modify/replace appears anywhere in the inserted or retained language (Section 19.4's refund is a warranty remedy, not an IP-indemnity remedy).

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x annual fees super-cap was added; Section 21.3 continues to place "indemnification obligations" outside the liability cap.

verification.notes: Preferred level is complete: the inserted paragraph delivers the defend-and-indemnify duty for Customer and its Affiliates, all four covered limbs (IP infringement of Services/Deliverables, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), the notice/control/cooperation mechanics, and an express cap on Customer's own indemnity to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law. Fallback level is incomplete (procure/modify/replace, refund backstop and 3x super-cap all absent), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is fully met and a super-cap would be a step down from Section 21.3, which currently leaves indemnification obligations uncapped. Minimal: a single concise insertion in the vacant Section 20 slot after Section 19.5, no deletions or paraphrase of retained text, no survival tail, at-own-expense language, extra damages categories or other model-language extras beyond the selected elements; the drafter correctly refrained from importing fallback-only remedies and a super-cap. Preserves intent: Sections 9.3, 19.4, 19.5, 21.3 and 30.5 all presuppose an indemnity and now have an operative referent; nothing retained contradicts the new clause and the Excluded Claims carve-out for indemnification obligations continues to operate. Repair note (not a failure of the checklist): Section 9.3's cross-reference to "Section 20.5" remains dangling because the pre-existing Section 20 is absent and the inserted text supplies no procure/modify/replace/refund remedy. Either renumber/insert those remedies as Section 20.5 or conform Section 9.3's cross-reference to the new indemnity section so the termination trigger is not inoperable. Drafting check: confirm the inserted paragraph carries its section number (rendered text appears unnumbered) and that "Affiliates", "Customer Data" and "Deliverables" are defined in Section 1; if any is undefined, add the definition to avoid an undefined capitalised term.

quote: 18.1 Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.
rationale: Section 18 satisfies the preferred position in full: CGL at USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, professional E&O at USD 2M, cyber and privacy liability at USD 5M (granted unconditionally, so it necessarily covers Vendor's processing of Customer Data), workers' compensation as required by law, and certificates of insurance on request under 18.2. Coverage runs through the term plus one year, and 18.2 confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities, so there is no offsetting give-back. Nothing elsewhere in the document narrows these limits or the data scope. No redline required.
